neighbours.label: describing how the body is held or carried: posture and bearing of shoulders, arms, back and gait
fire: The soldier stood rigidly at attention, shoulders squared and arms straight.
Tired after the match, the boy slouched in his chair with his arms dangling.
She walked into the room with her head high and her back very straight.
Roll your shoulders down and away from your ears as you breathe out.
The old farmer leaned on the gate, hunched over, hands hanging loose.
He strode across the stage with a confident, loose-limbed swagger.
Sit with your spine tall and let your arms rest at your sides.
The dancer held her arms out wide, shoulders low and relaxed.
quiet: The soldier had surgery on his shoulder after the training accident.
Tired after the match, the boy asked his mother for a sandwich.
She walked into the room and handed out the printed agendas.
The doctor ordered an X-ray of her right shoulder and elbow.
The old farmer fixed the gate and painted it green.
He bought a jacket two sizes larger than his usual one.
Measure your arm length before ordering a new wetsuit online.
The dancer booked a flight to Vienna for the competition.
